This answers the STRUCTURAL question both app-design sessions put to him on 2026-09-23: extract the shared scaffold into its own PRD, or merge the two app PRDs. He chose extract.

Its accepted recommendations (last-writer-wins on record_id; SQLite past a few thousand records) are in this design; RO-Crate was declined with a stated reason. A third scan over extracted text would restate them. This is a recorded decision with named prior work, not a skipped step.

The CAC's own unfilled <fill:> seams in the id-normalization helper and the contract-version gate mechanics. p0c implements the documented behaviour; the rest will be settled by reading FJ's or genKnown's interop.py.

Whether 'official app in KOROS' means code contributed upstream into koros/king or our repo conforming to the CAC. Open for both consumers; does not bind this module under either reading, since the consume-only interlock means it never contributes upstream.

Whether re-runs should collapse to one row. record_id derives from kind + subject + significant_params, so an identical re-run replaces its predecessor and history is lost. The parent PRD flagged the counter-argument and did not resolve it; carried forward unresolved rather than quietly settled by extraction.

round_1.S11_note: THE BEST FIND, AND MY FIRST RESOLUTION OF IT WAS WRONG. The adversary spotted that 'hard-fail on major, warn on compatible minor' contradicts 'contract_version is an INTEGER'. I first wrote that there is no minor. Checking king/docs/CROSS_APP_COMMUNICATION.md showed the contradiction is UPSTREAM: the wire field is ruled an integer at :141/:173/:252, section F states semver gating at :290, and :294 marks the gate mechanics an explicit unfilled placeholder. Final resolution: implement integer comparison only -- equal proceeds, any difference hard-fails -- and implement no minor branch, because with an integer on the wire there is nothing to compare a minor against. Propagated into BOTH consumer apps, whose tasks required the warn-on-minor behaviour.

round_2.character: Almost none were design objections; they were PRECISION gaps -- exactly what a module whose guarantee is 'two implementations and two producers agree exactly' should be attacked for. Round 1 found holes; round 2 found imprecision. Both were worth the round trip.
two_folds_that_improved_the_design_rathe: S18: FLOATS ARE NOW REJECTED in significant_params. The adversary recommended specifying a float FORMAT. Pinning one does not stop 0.1+0.2, a JSON round-trip and another language's parser differing in the last bit while every producer believes it complies. Rejecting floats forces a producer with a float parameter to format it to a string itself, which is the precision decision that should not be made silently inside a hash function.

S43: unknown_kind became a SMALL INTEGER (0 known, 1 well-formed but unregistered, 2 malformed) rather than a boolean. Non-zero still means unknown so no existing rule changes, but a consumer can now tell a peer app's new kind from a producer bug. Round 1's S5 had conflated them.
rejected_on_evidence: S31 constraining status transitions -- it would forbid the failed-to-ok retry the whole retry guarantee exists for.
S44 validating producer_version -- producers ship git SHAs and dates; a version this module cannot parse is still a version.

S29 rejecting payloads over 64KB -- THE REJECTION MATTERS: the write path fails soft, so a rejected write is logged and DROPPED, and a producer whose payload innocently grew would lose records silently. It warns and stores instead. A hard limit on a fail-soft path is a silent-data-loss generator.

hunks.location: Q9 bullet 1 -- KBDL object store reachability
hunks.chris: YES - it is and it always will be, so if that helps the design use it.
hunks.disposition: Folded into the artifacts URI vocabulary section and removed from could-not-decide. Changes NOTHING in this module -- the store validates the SHAPE of a ref and never resolves one -- but it removes the reason both consumer apps treated object-store artifacts as a degrade path. Said so plainly rather than manufacturing a change here to look responsive.

hunks.location: Q9 bullet 3 -- official app in KOROS
hunks.chris: I want it to show up as an app in KIND. I assume this involves some kind of deploy step that registers the apps in KIND?
hunks.disposition: Folded into Out of Scope: registration, not upstream contribution, which confirms the design as built and CLOSES this question for all three PRDs. His return question answered from source, not asserted: KING loads *.json from its plugins dir AT REQUEST TIME, so a manifest with type app registers with no restart and no KING code change (king_backend/plugins.py; APP_INTEGRATION.md:91; config.py:117-127). That step belongs to the two apps, not to this library.
hunks.side_finding: Checking it surfaced dev 1294: BOTH app PRDs write their manifest to ~/kind-apps/plugins/, which appears NOWHERE in the king stack, and plugins.py _load() swallows every error so the failure is silent. Filed, not fixed -- it belongs to two PRDs Chris submits after this one.

hunks.location: Q9 bullet 4 -- whether re-runs collapse to one row
hunks.chris: No - it should not, so runs should be dated and ideally grouped in the interace, and critically you should be able to delete a run from the database if you decide for example that an older run isn't useful. The apps should offer this kind of delete interface and the underlying data API should support it.
hunks.disposition: THE ROUND'S REAL WORK. Identity SPLIT into analysis_id (round 0's derivation, unchanged, now the GROUPING key) and record_id (per run, sha256(analysis_id + NUL + run_uid), run_uid required). delete_record(record_id) -> bool added, hard, cascading to the blob. DDL gains analysis_id, run_uid and an index on (analysis_id, created_at DESC). Propagated through: the Solution interface and honesty spine, user stories 5/5a/5b/5c, Implementation Decisions (interface, DDL, a rewritten identity section, a new delete section), S6 (an upsert is now a RETRY, and the two ids are immutable), Testing Decisions, gotchas G5/G13/G14, acceptance criteria 42-51, and the p0b and p0d task prompts and success criteria. New entry Q10, IRREVERSIBLE, sorted up with Q1-Q3.
hunks.why_the_retry_guarantee_survives: Re-recording the same record_id still replaces -- that is now a RETRY of one run, which is what the guarantee was always for. A RE-RUN is a different run_uid, hence a different record_id, hence a new dated row. Nothing negotiated with the twin session was broken; every addition is additive and existing call sites stay correct.
